remarks: Uttar Pradesh does not appear to have a dedicated Factories Act portal separate from its general industrial single-window system: Factory License ('Registration and grant of license under The Factories Act 1948') is one of 421 services listed on Nivesh Mitra, issued by the Labour Department, with a stated 30-day timeline under the 'Pre-Establishment' category.

The state's own Labour Department domains (labour.up.nic.in and uplabour.gov.in) — which secondary sources and even Nivesh Mitra's own checklist page cite as the authoritative home for the UP Factories Rules 1950 and the Factory License checklist — were both unreachable from this session (502 gateway error / connection reset). This matches the spec's expectation that some official sites will not be reachable via this fetch method; they are listed in `excluded` rather than fabricated or guessed.

Two parallel live versions of the state portal were found and verified: Nivesh Mitra 2.0 (niveshmitra.up.nic.in, the fuller/older system with the services catalog and checklist page) and Nivesh Mitra 3.0 (niveshmitra.up.gov.in, newer, but its own banner states some services are still only on 2.0). Both were included since either could be the operative one depending on when this list is used.

No official UP-government-hosted copy of the Factories Act 1948 / Uttar Pradesh Factories Rules 1950 full text could be independently verified this session; the only full-text copies found via search are on third-party legal-database sites (Indian Kanoon, LegitQuest) or on a Uttarakhand High Court PDF that is now 404. These were not included since they are not the state's own government source and/or failed verification.

invest.up.gov.in was included despite its main content area being a JS-rendered app shell, because curl still returned substantial real, on-topic static content (title, meta description, and a full genuine navigation menu matching the known structure of the official Invest UP site) — this was judged to be short of the spec's 'empty shell with no visible text' exclusion bar, unlike Sitemap.aspx and NOC_Search.aspx which were excluded.

All PDF candidates were opened and inspected beyond just HTTP 200: G_1.pdf was checked via pdftotext (readable embedded Hindi text), and G_2.pdf (a scanned, non-text PDF) was additionally rendered to a PNG image and visually read to confirm it is a genuine, legible official Government Order letter rather than a corrupt or blank scan.
